_about: Where a ship picture's engines are, when ThrusterFx's finder (the rearmost pixels, ThrusterFx.for_sprite) gets it wrong. Keyed by the picture's file name without .png; coordinates in that picture's own pixels (the full-size file; a _half picture halves them). Each engine is a column x and rows y0..y1: every row finds the hull's back edge from x (forward through plating to the first open pixel, or back through open space to the plating) and the flame starts on that edge -- ON the hull's 1 px dark outline where it has one, so it leaves the nozzle flush. Rows cover the whole opening (the contiguous rows whose edge is within 2 px of the deepest); ThrusterGallery checks the flame's start height against it. An empty list is a ship with no flame at all. Hand-placed Oct 13 off Jon's gallery verdicts; read each picture before adding one.

ship_asteroidtow.why: the tug's own engine; the rock it tows is the rearmost thing in the picture

ship_bigdish.why: the lit tail engine only, a 3-row port in a flat stern (port: its own opening); the dish rim reaches further back

ship_scoop.why: the drive pod under the hull, its whole rear end (port: the prong above is not the nozzle); the scoop prong tips reach further back

hulk_honeycomb.why: the centre tail engine, its whole face: Jon found the 4-row flame too small; the fins either side are fins

hulk_rs_net.why: the hull's own stern between the net's fins

lancer_solarsail.why: the hull's rounded stern between the sails, not the sail tips

cutter_swarm.why: the whole flat stern plate; the finder took the antenna rod's tip

ship_cl_stack.why: bottom thruster pod; the pipe loop behind is not an engine

ship_courier2.why: the lower thruster block, not the tail wing

ship_fm_domes.why: the thruster cylinder on top, its whole rear cap (Jon: the flame did not fit the nozzle)

ship_mkt_slung.why: top thruster pod at the back
bottom thruster pod at the back (port: the pod rear, not the hull above it)
